entities.summary: Luiz Gonzaga do Nascimento was a Brazilian singer, songwriter, musician and poet and one of the most influential figures of Brazilian popular music in the twentieth century. He has been credited with having presented the rich universe of Northeastern musical genres to all of Brazil, having popularized the musical genre baião and has been called a "revolutionary" by Antônio Carlos Jobim. According to Caetano Veloso, he was the first significant cultural event with mass appeal in Brazil. Luiz Gonzaga received the Shell prize for Brazilian Popular Music in 1984 and was only the fourth artist to receive this prize after Pixinguinha, Antônio Carlos Jobim and Dorival Caymmi.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Luiz Gonzaga's influence on Brazilian popular music helped shape a continental era, with his work in Northeastern musical genres being credited as a key cultural event with mass appeal in Brazil. His recognition by the Shell prize for Brazilian Popular Music in 1984 solidified his impact on the country's music scene.
